paramHints.minPurge: Minimum purge on the wipe tower at a filament change - how much to extrude to clear the previous colour from the nozzle.
paramHints.loadSpeedStart: Speed at the start of filament loading (first millimetres). Usually slower than the main speed so the strand feeds in cleanly.
paramHints.loadSpeed: Main filament loading speed at a change.
paramHints.unloadSpeedStart: Speed at the start of unloading (a tug to break free). Usually faster than the main speed.
paramHints.unloadSpeed: Main filament unloading speed at a change.
paramHints.toolchangeDelay: Pause after unloading before loading the new filament - lets the melt drain so it doesn't string.
paramHints.coolingMoves: How many back-and-forth moves shape the filament tip on unload. More moves = a cleaner tip.
paramHints.coolingInitialSpeed: Speed of the first cooling move while shaping the filament tip.
paramHints.coolingFinalSpeed: Speed of the last cooling move - usually faster, as the tip has already set.
paramHints.stampingLoadSpeed: Loading speed during tip stamping. 0 disables the feature.
paramHints.stampingDistance: Distance for stamping the filament tip. 0 = off.
paramHints.multitoolRamming: Enable ramming (a quick purge before a change) for a multi-extruder printer. Shapes the filament tip.
paramHints.multitoolRammingVolume: Ramming volume for a multi-extruder printer - how much plastic to extrude while shaping the tip.
paramHints.multitoolRammingFlow: Ramming flow (volumetric rate) for a multi-extruder printer.
paramHints.filamentChangeLength: Ramming length at a filament change - how much to extrude/retract to shape the tip. 0 = as set in the printer.
paramHints.adaptivePA: Automatically tunes Pressure Advance to speed/flow from a calibration model. Removes bulges on accelerations without calibrating per speed. Beta.
paramHints.adaptivePAOverhangs: Extend adaptive Pressure Advance to overhangs too, where flow changes sharply. Beta.
paramHints.adaptivePABridges: Pressure Advance value used for bridges in adaptive mode. Bridges print at a fixed PA.
paramHints.adaptivePAMeasured: Calibration data for adaptive Pressure Advance: flow→PA pairs the model is built from. Filled in from calibration results.
paramHints.adhesiveness: Material adhesion category (for Bambu's algorithms). Affects which build surfaces are considered compatible. Optional.
paramHints.zHop: Lifts the nozzle (along Z) during a retraction so it clears printed parts while travelling. 0 = no lift.
paramHints.deretractionSpeed: Speed of pushing filament back (unretract) after a retraction. Usually equal to or slightly below the retraction speed.
paramHints.zHopType: How the Z axis lifts on retraction: normal, spiral, or auto. Affects travel speed and Z wear.
paramHints.liftEnforce: Which surfaces the Z lift applies to: everywhere, top only, or nowhere.
paramHints.liftAbove: Lift the nozzle only when the current print height is above this value. 0 = no limit.
paramHints.liftBelow: Lift the nozzle only when the current print height is below this value. 0 = no limit.
paramHints.retractRestartExtra: Extra filament pushed after a retraction to restore pressure. Usually 0; positive fights under-extrusion, negative fights blobs.
paramHints.retractMinTravel: Minimum travel length that triggers a retraction. Short hops skip it - less wear.
paramHints.retractOnLayerChange: Retract when moving to a new layer. Reduces the seam blob at the layer change.
paramHints.wipe: Move the nozzle over printed material during a retraction to wipe off residue and reduce stringing.
paramHints.wipeDistance: Length of the wipe move along the perimeter during a retraction.
paramHints.retractBeforeWipe: How much of the retraction happens before the wipe starts. 100% = all before wiping, 0% = during.
paramHints.retractAfterWipe: Share of retraction performed after wiping. Together with the before-wipe value it cannot exceed 100%.
paramHints.retractLengthToolchange: Retraction length used when switching material. This is separate from regular travel retraction.
paramHints.retractRestartExtraToolchange: Extra feed after a material-change retraction. Positive values compensate under-extrusion; negative values reduce blobs.
paramHints.retractDistanceCut: Retraction lengths for the filament-cut system (e.g. Bambu). Comma-separated per extruder.
paramHints.longRetractCut: Use a long retraction when cutting filament - pulls the strand further back for a clean cut.
paramHints.longRetractEC: Long retraction on extruder change (multi-extruder setups) - prevents oozing while a nozzle is idle.
paramHints.retractDistanceEC: How far to pull the filament back on an extruder change.
paramHints.closeFanFirstLayers: How many first layers print with the fan off. Early layers need to bond to the bed, and cooling works against that.
paramHints.initialLayerFanSpeed: Explicit first-layer fan speed. Available only when fan-off layers is 0; −1 disables the override.
paramHints.fullFanSpeedLayer: Layer by which the fan ramps up to full speed. Below it the speed climbs from the initial value. 0 = auto.
paramHints.minFanThreshold: Lower fan bound. If a layer takes longer than this time, the fan runs at this (minimum) speed.
paramHints.maxFanThreshold: Upper fan bound. If a layer prints faster than this time, the fan reaches this (maximum) speed. Between the thresholds the speed is interpolated.
paramHints.fanAlwaysOn: Keep the fan running between short moves instead of stopping it. Avoids RPM surges and keeps cooling steady.
paramHints.slowForCooling: Slow printing down when a layer prints too fast to cool. Helps small parts and overhangs.
paramHints.dontSlowOuterWall: Don't slow the outer wall even when cooling a layer - preserves the visible surface quality.
paramHints.minPrintSpeed: The slicer won't slow below this speed for cooling, even on a very short layer.
paramHints.overhangFan: Enable stronger cooling on overhangs and bridges. Sharply improves their quality, especially on PLA.
paramHints.overhangThreshold: How steep an overhang triggers the stronger fan. A lower percentage triggers earlier (by how unsupported the perimeter is).
paramHints.overhangFanSpeed: Fan speed on overhangs and outer bridges. −1 keeps it unchanged (no override).
paramHints.internalBridgeFanSpeed: Fan speed on internal bridges (spans over infill). −1 = no override.
paramHints.supportInterfaceFanSpeed: Fan speed on the support interface layer - makes supports easier to detach. −1 = no override.
paramHints.ironingFanSpeed: Fan speed during ironing of top surfaces. −1 = no override.
paramHints.auxiliaryFan: Extra (side/enclosure) part-cooling fan, if the printer has one. Runs alongside the main fan.
paramHints.exhaustFan: Chamber/filter exhaust fan. Useful during and after printing ABS/ASA to vent harmful fumes.
paramHints.soluble: Soluble material (PVA, BVOH): supports wash away in water instead of being broken off. Used for support interfaces in multi-material printing.
paramHints.supportMaterial: Material intended for printing supports. The slicer uses it for supports and their interface in multi-material printing.
paramHints.shrinkXY: Shrinkage compensation in the XY plane. The model is pre-scaled so it matches the target size after cooling. 100% means no compensation.
paramHints.shrinkZ: Shrinkage compensation along height (Z). Set separately from XY, since shrinkage across layers often differs from in-plane shrinkage.
paramHints.softeningTemp: Material softening temperature: above it the part starts to lose shape. Acts as a safe-chamber reference - Orca warns when it's exceeded.
paramHints.idleTemp: Nozzle temperature while idle (when the filament isn't printing, e.g. during a multi-material change). Keeps the plastic hot without letting it scorch in the nozzle.
paramHints.chamberTemp: An active chamber keeps the air around the part warm. Needed for ABS/ASA/PC (less warping and delamination); usually not needed for PLA/PETG.
paramHints.chamberMinimalTemp: Minimum chamber temperature exposed to start G-code or a heat-soak macro. It does not heat or wait by itself and cannot exceed the target temperature.
paramHints.adaptiveFlow: The slicer automatically lowers volumetric flow on areas where the nozzle can't melt fast enough. Avoids manual tuning of the limit.
paramHints.extruderTemp: Nozzle temperature while printing. Too low - weak layer bonding; too high - blobs and stringing. Start from the spool's stated range.
paramHints.extruderTempFirst: Nozzle temperature for the first layer. Often 5–10 °C higher than normal for better bed adhesion.
paramHints.bedTemp: Bed temperature - controls first-layer adhesion. Usually 50–60 °C for PLA, higher for PETG/ABS.
paramHints.bedTempFirst: Bed temperature for the first layer. Sometimes slightly higher than normal so the part grips the bed.
paramHints.flow: Filament flow multiplier. 1.0 is normal; lower it for over-extrusion, raise it for under-extrusion (gaps).
paramHints.retractionLength: How far filament is pulled back on travel moves - fights stringing and blobs. ~0.5–2 mm for direct drive, more for Bowden.
paramHints.retractionSpeed: How fast filament is retracted. Too high can click and grind the filament.
paramHints.fanSpeed: Part cooling fan. Cools layers: vital for PLA and small parts, but harmful for ABS (delamination).
paramHints.maxVolumetricSpeed: Max plastic per second the hotend can melt (mm³/s). This is the real cap on print speed.
paramHints.pressureAdvance: Compensates nozzle pressure - removes blobs at corners and line start/end. Needs calibration.
paramHints.diameter: Filament diameter. Almost always 1.75 mm; rarely 2.85 mm. Must match what's actually loaded.
paramHints.density: Material density (g/cm³). Needed to compute weight and print cost from filament length.
paramHints.nozzleHardness: How abrasive the material is. Composites (carbon, glass, glow-in-the-dark) wear a brass nozzle down — hardened steel is needed. HRC is the Rockwell hardness scale: brass below 50, hardened steel 50–60, ruby around 60, tungsten carbide 70 and above.

help.title: Workspace guide
help.presetsDesc: A preset connects one catalog filament with its print parameters. This tab contains your own, saved, and draft presets.
help.presetsStep1: Create a new preset or save a suitable preset from the catalog
help.presetsStep2: Link it to the exact filament so its brand, material, and color stay in context
help.presetsStep3: Enter working temperatures and essential print parameters; open advanced settings only when needed
help.presetsStep4: Version your own presets and use someone else's preset as a saved reference or your own copy
help.presetsNote: Import and export actions inside OrcaSlicer appear only when the installed host version grants the plugin those capabilities.
help.printersDesc: A physical printer and its OrcaSlicer configurations are different things. Here you connect the real machine to its machine and print profiles.
help.printersStep1: Add the physical printer and specify its model
help.printersStep2: Attach one or more machine configurations and the print-quality profiles you use
help.printersStep3: Configurations not yet attached to a machine remain in a separate section and are not lost
help.printersNote: Changing an address or connection provider must not create a new physical printer or erase its history.
help.spoolsDesc: Track your physical spools here: remaining material, state, price, lot, usage history, and assignment to a printer or material-system slot.
help.spoolsStep1: Add a spool and, whenever possible, link it to the exact catalog filament
help.spoolsStep2: Enter its initial weight, then correct usage manually or accept reports from a connected printer
help.spoolsStep3: Create a material system, choose its printer, and assign spools immediately; connection instructions appear inside the setup flow
help.calculatorDesc: A production workspace for costing, saved estimates, customers, quotes, and orders.
help.calculatorStep1: Upload G-code to extract print time and material usage, or enter the data manually
help.calculatorStep2: Configure recurring economics: equipment, electricity, labor, depreciation, and markup
help.calculatorStep3: Save the estimate, prepare a quote, and continue with the customer and order when needed
help.syncDesc: The FilamentHub plugin runs in official OrcaSlicer and syncs available presets and printer profiles without manual file transfers.
help.syncStep1: Go to "Settings" (gear icon) and enable the "OrcaSlicer Sync" toggle
help.syncStep2: On each preset, click the sync icon (🔄) to make it available in the slicer
help.syncStep3: Open official OrcaSlicer with the FilamentHub plugin installed — your presets will appear in the materials list
help.syncNote: Sync works both ways: changes in OrcaSlicer will also reflect on the website.
help.brandDesc: A verified brand representative manages its catalog data, official materials, and presets. FilamentHub is a data showcase, not a store.
help.brandStep1: Accept a brand invitation or submit a representation request
help.brandStep2: After approval, switch from the personal workspace to the company workspace
help.brandStep3: Maintain materials, official presets, QR codes, and brand details within your granted permissions
help.settingsDesc: Settings control your account, regional preferences, and available synchronization directions.
help.settingsStep1: Change your username or email and set or update a local password
help.settingsStep2: Choose interface language, catalog country, and calculation currency; these preferences do not declare citizenship
help.settingsStep3: Enable only the OrcaSlicer data flows you need; unavailable capabilities are marked separately
help.hhDesc: Happy Hare is firmware for MMU systems (ERCF, Box Turtle, etc.). FilamentHub integrates via the Spoolman protocol: assign spools to gates on the website, and the printer picks up changes automatically.
help.hhConnectStep1: Find spoolman_support and set it to: pull
help.hhConnectStep2: Find t_macro_color and set it to: gatemap
help.hhConnectStep3: Set your FilamentHub URL as the Spoolman endpoint (API key - in Profile Settings → Sync)

tooltips.junctionDeviation: Controls how much paths are rounded through corners. Lower values hold corners more accurately but can slow the printer more; higher values smooth turns more aggressively and may increase ringing.
tooltips.singleExtruderMultiMaterial: SEMM stands for Single Extruder Multi Material. Use it when multiple materials or colors share one hotend and are fed through it one after another instead of using separate nozzles.
tooltips.bedTemperatureFormula: Chooses which loaded filament drives the bed temperature in multi-material prints: the first filament or the one with the highest bed-temperature requirement.
tooltips.wipeTower: A wipe tower is a sacrificial structure printed next to the part. It receives purge material during color or material changes so the previous material does not contaminate the model.
tooltips.purgeInPrimeTower: When enabled, purge and cleaning moves during material changes are sent into the wipe tower instead of the model or open air.
tooltips.ramming: Ramming shapes the filament tip before unloading by compressing molten material in a controlled way. This reduces jams and stringy tips during material changes.
tooltips.toolChangeOnWipeTower: For multi-tool printers, move to the wipe tower before issuing the tool-change command so the swap does not happen above the model.
tooltips.semm: This block tunes loading and unloading behavior for SEMM workflows: how far to retract, where to stop the filament in the cooling tube, and how much extra push to apply on reload.
tooltips.parkingRetraction: How far the filament retracts before parking or switching. This helps release pressure in the hotend before unloading or waiting.
tooltips.coolingTubeRetraction: The target filament position inside the cooling tube before the rest of the unload sequence continues. It strongly affects how repeatable the filament tip shape is.
tooltips.coolingTubeLength: The effective cooling tube length in the unload path. If this is wrong, the slicer will mistime where the tip is formed.
tooltips.extraLoadingMove: An extra push after the main load move. Useful when the filament needs a little more travel to reliably reach the melt zone.
tooltips.toolChangeTime: A slicer-side estimate for how long a tool or material change takes. It affects time calculation and planning, not the printer mechanics directly.

nozzleGuide.title: Nozzle material guide
nozzleGuide.caption: Use this as a selection aid. Final temperatures and speed still depend on the hotend, the specific filament, and the vendor profile for that material.

brass.temperature: Baseline reference for PLA, PETG, and other non-abrasive materials. Usually does not need extra temperature versus the profile.
brass.speed: Best everyday heat transfer balance for standard print speeds and typical flow.

hardened_steel.temperature: Often needs a small bump compared with brass because thermal transfer is lower.
hardened_steel.speed: Strong all-round choice, but at very high speeds it usually carries less heat than copper or carbide.

stainless_steel.temperature: Usually works with a slight increase over brass temperatures, especially on more viscous materials.
stainless_steel.speed: Better kept at moderate speeds; not the strongest option for aggressive high-flow setups.

tungsten_carbide.temperature: Typically stays stable across the working range and keeps flow consistent even on hotter engineering materials.
tungsten_carbide.speed: Well suited to faster printing and higher flow if the rest of the extrusion path can keep up.

copper_alloy.temperature: High thermal transfer helps with hotter materials, but the exact window still depends on coating and nozzle construction.
copper_alloy.speed: Works well for increased flow as long as the nozzle is not a soft copper design intended only for non-abrasive use.

ruby.temperature: Usually stable across normal printing temperatures, but the nozzle should not be stressed by crashes or misalignment.
ruby.speed: Normal to moderately high speeds are fine when the machine is well aligned and mechanically stable.

titanium.temperature: Lower thermal transfer can require a higher setpoint or a more conservative material profile.
titanium.speed: Usually better for calmer print speeds and controlled flow than for chasing maximum throughput.

nickel_plated_copper.temperature: Handles hotter materials well and often supports more stable feeding near the upper end of the temperature range.
nickel_plated_copper.speed: A good fit for higher-flow printing when the specific model has enough wear resistance for the job.

E3D.temperature: This is an Orca vendor bucket rather than a single material. Check the actual nozzle material in the spec for that model.
E3D.speed: Speed behavior depends on the exact E3D nozzle family: standard, hardened, ObXidian, High Flow, and so on.

general.title: 1. General Provisions
paragraphs: 1.1. This Privacy Policy (hereinafter referred to as the Policy) defines the procedure for processing and protecting personal data of users of the FilamentHub service (hereinafter referred to as the Service), available at filamenthub.ru.
1.2. The personal data operator is Kuzmin I.I., an individual applying the special tax regime “Tax on Professional Income” (NPD taxpayer). Contact email address: support@filamenthub.ru.
1.3. The Policy is developed in accordance with Federal Law No. 152-FZ dated July 27, 2006 “On Personal Data” and other regulatory legal acts of the Russian Federation.

1.4. This Policy is an informational document and does not itself replace a separate consent to personal data processing. Viewing public pages of the Service does not constitute acceptance of the Terms of Service or provision of such consent.
1.5. The Service may be used by individuals who have reached the age of 14 and by legal entities.

dataCollected.title: 2. Data We Collect
dataCollected.intro: 2.1. The following categories of personal data are processed when using the Service:
categories: Email address, login, and data necessary for registration, sign-in, account recovery, and account security;
Full name (only if voluntarily provided by the User);
Profile data provided voluntarily: avatar and the country selected by the User for regional features;
Data provided when applying for brand verification (brand name, corporate email, website, social media links, supporting documents);
Personal library data and Service settings: spools, printers, material systems, presets, profiles, calculations, and history of related actions;
Materials published by the User, including reviews, ratings, profiles, and other community content;
Support requests and other correspondence with the Operator, including sender and recipient addresses, message content, delivery metadata, and attachments when submitted;

Technical data: IP address, the current network connection country derived from it, user-agent, request date and time, and service identifiers. The connection country is used only to select available sign-in methods and security measures and is not treated as citizenship or profile country;
Printing settings when using the synchronization function: material presets, printer profiles, print profiles, and technical parameters.
dataCollected.oauth: 2.2. When a third-party sign-in method is available for the current network connection and the User initiates sign-in through Google or Yandex, we receive the email address, name, and user identifier within the permissions granted.

purposes.title: 3. Purposes of Data Processing
purposes.intro: 3.1. Personal data is processed for the following purposes:
items: Registration and authorization of the user on the Service;
Selecting available sign-in methods and registration safeguards based on the current network connection country;
Providing Service functionality (materials catalog, presets, calculator, OrcaSlicer synchronization);
Verification of brand and manufacturer representatives;
Sending service notifications (email confirmation, password reset, system notifications);
Ensuring Service security and protection against abuse;
User support, error diagnostics, improving Service quality, and analyzing its operation, including through aggregated metrics.
purposes.note: 3.2. The Operator may send necessary service messages, replies to requests, and other communications permitted by applicable law and the User’s selected settings.
purposes.legalBasis: 3.3. Depending on the operation, processing is based on the User’s separate consent, steps requested by the User to enter into or perform the Terms of Service, the Operator’s legal obligations, or another basis provided by law. During OAuth, minimum data is processed to complete the sign-in requested by the User; personal features remain unavailable until the terms and consent are separately confirmed.

thirdParty.title: 4. Third-Party Services
thirdParty.intro: 4.1. To ensure the operation of the Service, we use the following third-party services to which certain data may be transferred:
services: Google OAuth (Google Ireland Limited / Google LLC, Ireland / USA) - sign-in through a Google account when this method is available for the current network connection and selected by the User. A request is made to obtain the user’s email and basic profile. Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy
Yandex OAuth (Yandex LLC, Russia) - authorization via Yandex account. A request is made to obtain the user’s email and basic profile. Yandex Privacy Policy: https://yandex.ru/legal/confidential/

The script is not loaded during ordinary viewing of public pages. Technical data is transmitted for verification. Google Privacy Policy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Yandex Cloud Postbox (Yandex.Cloud LLC, Russia) - delivery of service messages and outgoing addressed correspondence. Delivery requires sender and recipient addresses, subject, content, attachments, and technical delivery data. Incoming correspondence is received and stored in the Russian data perimeter.
thirdParty.note: 4.2. These services process data in accordance with their own privacy policies. We do not transfer any data to these services beyond the minimum necessary for the operation of the respective function.

crossBorder.title: 5. Cross-Border Data Transfer
paragraphs: 5.1. In connection with the use of third-party services (Section 4), necessary data may be transferred to Ireland (EU), the USA, and other jurisdictions where the relevant providers and their processors operate.
5.2. Data transfer is carried out exclusively to the extent necessary to provide Service functionality (authorization, bot protection, delivery of service emails).
5.3. The conditions and legal basis for such transfers are determined with regard to applicable law and the specifics of the relevant function.

5.4. Where a particular operation requires separate User consent or another lawful basis, the Operator obtains it before performing that operation. Use of the Service alone is not treated as separate consent to a cross-border transfer.

retention.title: 6. Data Retention and Deletion
paragraphs: 6.1. Personal data is retained no longer than required for the processing purposes, operation of the account, protection of the parties’ rights and legitimate interests, and mandatory legal requirements.
6.2. The User may delete their account independently through the personal account interface or by sending a request to support@filamenthub.ru.

6.3. When an account is deleted, private identifiers and account data are deleted or anonymized in accordance with applicable law. Published community materials may be retained without a link to the deleted account unless otherwise required by law or the User’s rights.

6.4. Limited data may remain temporarily in backups, security logs, and records that must be retained by law, with restrictions on purpose and retention period. Inactive accounts may be deleted after prior notice where reasonably practicable.

security.title: 7. Data Security

7.2. Such measures include access controls, protection of credentials, encryption in transit, and other safeguards appropriate to the nature and risks of processing.
7.3. The Operator maintains the confidentiality of personal data and discloses it only where a lawful basis exists. No method of transmission or storage can guarantee absolute security.
